text:
Macklin Celebrini played a career-high 28:05 on Saturday, on the second half of a back-to-back, and the Sharks still lost their fifth straight. That one number is the season in miniature: the young star is doing everything, and the structure around him isn't ready for it. San Jose is 7-11-1, outscored 22-8 during the skid, and the chances back the result (40 percent of the expected goals, the measure of chance quality).

The penalty kill is the worst of it. The Sharks give up 1.06 expected goals a game shorthanded, and Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest counted five power-play goals against in the last two games. The Darnell Nurse and Michael Kesselring pair, which plays the most, has been outscored 11-3. Will Smith has been talking openly about the power play's struggles too.

There are reasons to keep watching. Celebrini keeps scoring through the losses, Filip Bystedt's debut came in a comeback win over Vancouver, and the Smith, Celebrini and Igor Chernyshov line takes 62 percent of the chances when it's together. Alexander Wennberg, with three points in nine on chances worth six, is due for some puck luck. Our simulations put San Jose's playoff odds at 4 percent. The point of this season is growth, and the 28-minute nights are a sign of who the franchise is built around, for better and for worse.
headline: Celebrini is carrying San Jose, and it shows
